MINUTES
  ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION
  MARCH 14, 2023

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

An adjourned meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
at 12:09 p.m. in the Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by MAYOR HUFF.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by MAYOR HUFF.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura and Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Senior Accountant Fernando Estrada
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson
  Administrative Aide Gabrielle Swain

4.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  “FIRST LOOK” FOR THE RESIDENCES AT PENINSULA SHOPPING CENTER
  PROJECT

Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton introduced the Residences at Peninsula
Shopping Center Project, and welcomed Jeff Axtell, Executive Vice President and Ryan Ash, Vice
President of Development of Vestar, who provided a high-level presentation of Vestar
Communities, the residential component of the Peninsula Center project.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ thanked Vestar for their thoughtful development for both the retailers
and the community.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN encouraged Vestar to use the words “workforce housing’ and
“affordable housing” interchangeably and hopes the amount of workforce housing will be more than
the proposed 5%.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA echoed COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN’S comments, stating
she also hopes to see more than 5% of workforce housing. Consultant Ash confirmed that the
housing will all be “for-rent”, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA.

Architect Paul Kearney of MVE + Partners, Senior Designer of the project provided a presentation
of renderings of the design aspect of the proposed project.

MAYOR PRO TEM SCHMITZ made positive comments about the presented design plan and
stated that she hopes to see more trees throughout the development.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN stated he was excited to see the project come to fruition and
hopes to see more opportunity for workforce housing.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
MARCH 14, 2023 (PDS)
 COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA confirmed that no businesses will be displaced for the construction
of this property, which was confirmed by Consultant Ash. COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA also
echoed COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN’S sentiments regarding more workforce housing. She
confirmed that the City’s sustainability goals will be included in the design and construction of the
building.

It was the general consensus of the City Council to support additional parking for Palos Verdes
Performing Arts/Norris Theatre, to provide connectivity with the adjacent Promenade, and to see
more workforce housing included in the plans.

5.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATION

MAYOR HUFF introduced Library Board of Trustee Jonathan Beutler, who mentioned upcoming
events for the Library District, including the opening of the Teen Annex at the Peninsula Center
Library on April 6, and Doors Open Peninsula on June 17.

A.  HdL COMPANIES PRESENTATION ON PROPERTY TAX TRENDS, SALES TAX
  OUTLOOK AND BUSINESS LICENSE ADMINISTRATION

Administrative Services Director Whitehead introduced Bobby Young, Nichole Cone and Eric
Meyers of HdL Companies, who provided an update on the current state of the City’s Sales Tax,
Property Taxes and Business Licenses:

  -  RHE Sales Tax Rate Breakdown
  -  Statewide Sales Tax Trends and Major Industry Groups
  -  Inflation and Sales Tax and Current conditions
  -  Interest Rates and California Unemployment
  -  HdL Statewide Trend Quarterly Outlook and Annual Outlook for Sales Tax
  -  Allocation of Countywide Use Tax Pool
  -  Online sales allocations
  -  Proposition 13
  -  RHE Property Tax Dollar Breakdown
  -  Historical Assessed Value Growth and Single-Family Residential Sales History
  -  Business Tax Operation – Compliance, Collections and Discovery

B.  PENSION FUNDING POLICY PRESENTATION BY  MARK  YOUNG,  KNN
  CONSULTING, AND DAN MATUSIEWICZ, GOVINVEST

Senior Accountant Estrada introduced Mark Young of KNN Consulting and Dan Matusiewicz of
GovInvest, who presented a pension funding update for the City, and the proposed Pension
Funding Policy for the Council’s consideration.

Discussion ensued regarding the proposed Pension Funding Policy.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL
  VOTE:

  APPROVED THE PROPOSED PENSION FUNDING POLICY

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura and Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

6.  ITEMS FOR DISCUSSION

A.  POLICY DEVELOPMENT SESSION ITEMS

  Recommendation: That the City Council consider the items presented and prioritize them
  on the work plan for the coming fiscal year.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
MARCH 14, 2023 (PDS)
 ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES DEPARTMENT

  MID-YEAR BUDGET REVIEW

Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda material),
summarizing a review of the City’s budget for fiscal year 2022-23 at mid-year.

This item is informational for the Council.

  FISCAL HEALTH REPORT, FY 2012-13 THROUGH FY 2021-22

Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda material),
summarizing the Fiscal Health Report which covers a ten-year period and includes the audited
financial results reported in the annually prepared Comprehensive Financial Report (ACFR).

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by MAYOR HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  RECEIVE AND FILE THE FISCAL HEALTH REPORT.

  AYES:  Brown Schachter, Huff, Schmitz, Stegura and Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  None

  FINANCE UPDATE

Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda material),
summarizing the City’s Sales Tax, Property Taxes and Business Licenses.

This item is informational for the Council.

  AMENDMENTS TO BUSINESS LICENSE TAX CHAPTER

City Attorney Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), related to a Resolution
conditioned on the approval of Measure A in 2018, regarding pro-ration of taxes for fixed location
business that only operated in the City for a portion of the year.

Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to bring
back an ordinance that would repeal Section 5.04.180 of the Municipal Code and thereby
eliminate all pro-rations as that was the intent when the City moved to a flat tax schedule.

  INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY UPDATE

Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda material),
providing an update on the City’s information technology (IT), Wi-Fi, voice and data services,
cellular, hardware, security, monitoring, and advanced technical support.

This item is informational for the Council.

ADMINISTRATION DEPARTMENT

  COYOTE MANAGEMENT

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), summarizing
the City’s administration of protocols in coordination with the Los Angeles County Agricultural
Commissioner/Weighs department for coyote education and responses in the City, while also
noting that Staff will be further exploring contracting for emergency coyote management services
in the new fiscal year should the County have any staff changes that affect service to the City.

This item is informational for the Council.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
MARCH 14, 2023 (PDS)
 ***ITEM TAKEN OUT OF ORDER**

  MAYOR AND MAYOR PRO TEM ROTATION POLICY

City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), summarizing the
informal yet longstanding policy for rotating through the Council positions of Mayor and Mayor
Pro Tem, which was last reviewed by the City Council in 2016.

Following discussion, no changes were made to the current informal policy.

  ANIMAL LICENSING FEES AND EXPENSES

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), gauging the
City Council’s interest in exploring cost recovery options to help with future cost recovery, such
as direct resident billing for extraordinary circumstances, no or low-cost micro-chipping,
vaccination and licensing clinics, increasing dog licensing fees and consideration of requiring
cat licensing (which is currently voluntary).

Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to proceed with direct
resident billing for extraordinary circumstances, direction to consider no or low-cost
micro-chipping, vaccination and licensing clinics, and direction to maintain current fees.

  WASTE MANAGEMENT

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), discussing
Waste Management’s request to the City to consider modifying its service schedule from one
day per week to multiple days per week.

Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to convene the Waste
Subcommittee to assess the Waste Management request and, if needed negotiate terms,
for a final review by the City Council.

  PURCHASE OF TRAIL VEHICLES FOR SHERRIFF’S PATROL

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), discussing
the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department – Lomita Station’s (LASD-Lomita) request for the
purchase of off-road vehicles (ATVs), noting that the current off-road vehicle, Polaris, is currently
at its useful life expectancy and that its large size is not suitable for some city trails.

Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to look into
the idea of a volunteer group to monitor the trails on horseback and provide education,
while also having staff look into possible grants for the purchase of off-road vehicles,
trailer and safety equipment.

  PROPOSED SBCCOG DUES INCREASE

City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), summarizing the
proposed due increase and the COG’s new formulations of those dues.

This item is informational for the Council.

COMMUNITY SERVICES DEPARTMENT

  SPORTS FIELD POLICY

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), summarizing
the results of the sports field use study the City conducted, and the need for a Sports Field
Policy.

This item is informational for the Council.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
MARCH 14, 2023 (PDS)
   TENNIS COURT CLEANING

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda material),
summarizing that currently the courts are cleaned only on an emergency basis, and that in order
to maintain and extend the life of the new resurfacing, staff is recommending the courts be
professionally cleaned on a regular basis.

Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to budget
for bi-annual tennis court cleaning in the amount of $7,700 and an additional amount of
$3,000 for emergency court cleaning.

  IRRIGATION STUDY

Maintenance Supervisor Goldsmith provided a staff report (as per the agenda material),
summarizing the irrigation audit of the City parks performed by WaterWise Consulting.

Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to include this irrigation
upgrade project in in the City’s proposed upcoming two-year budget.

  CAPITAL PROJECTS

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), summarizing
the projects identified by staff and the Park & Activities Commission to be considered over the
next two fiscal years.

Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to direct staff to consider
items listed in the staff report for inclusion in the City’s proposed upcoming two-year
budget.

  “BUTCHER PROJECT” PROJECT STATUS

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), summarizing
the discussion and recommendation of the Park & Activities Commission for the naming of
“Butcher Park.”

Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to approve the name
“Founders Park.”

  NATURE CENTER

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), summarizing
the status of the project, noting that the project balance not currently funded or allocated is
estimated at $1.3 million and that staff is actively seeking other grants and partnerships to
support this project.

Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to allocate Park Facility
Fees to fund the balance of the project cost in coordination with additional grant funds
and donations.

  PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION OUTREACH AND FUNDRAISING

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), summarizing
that at the most recent Pepper Tree Fundraising Committee meeting, the Committee prioritized
fundraising for the new Nature Center and specifically, made recommendations for goals and
the design of a successful campaign to be considered by the City Council.

Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to consider limited naming
opportunities and a donor wall in order to meet to the fundraising goal, and return to the
City Council with a proposed fundraising program for the Nature Center.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), summarizing
staff’s efforts to improve the Pepper Tree Foundation page within the City current website making
it more visible and enhanced within the website’s capabilities

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
MARCH 14, 2023 (PDS)
 Following discussion, it was the consensus of the City Council to enhance the existing
Pepper Tree Foundation webpage content on the City’s current website to include drop
down menus highlighting various projects funded by the Foundation, utilizing Tripepi
Smith’s offer to donate time to create a project page template for the Armenian Genocide
public art project, which can be used by City staff to create other project pages

COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT

  DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS

Community Development Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material),
providing updates on the 927 Deep Valley Drive condominium project, the Peninsula Pointe
assisted living project, the Rolling Hills Country Club, and a proposed project at the Brickwalk
site.

This item is informational for the Council.

  LONG-RANGE PROJECTS AND PROGRAMS

Community Development Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material),
providing an update on the status of CA Department of Housing and Community Development
(HCD) regarding obtaining certification for the City’s Housing Element, as well as staff’s initiation
of the comprehensive update of the Zoning code, to implement the 2040 General Plan in March
2023.

This item is informational for the Council.

  CODE COMPLIANCE

Community Development Director Naughton provided a staff report (as per the agenda material),
providing an update on complaints frequently received by the City regarding trash cans being
left on the street for extended periods of time, and steps taken by staff to address these
complaints.

This item is informational for the Council.

PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT

  CAL WATER RESPONSE TO WATER MAIN BREAKS

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

This item is informational for the Council.

  SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA EDISON (SCE) TREE TRIMMING COORDINATION WITH
  CITY TREE TRIMMING

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

This item is informational for the Council.

B.  MID-YEAR REPORTS

  Recommendation: That the City Council receive and file these reports.

It was the consensus of the City Council to receive and file the mid-year reports.

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
MARCH 14, 2023 (PDS)
 5.  ADJOURNMENT

At 5:20 p.m. MAYOR HUFF adjourned the City Council meeting to the Regular City Council
meeting scheduled for Tuesday, March 28, 2023 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers at Rolling
Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Britt Huff
City Clerk  Mayor

ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
MARCH 14, 2023 (PDS)
